title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed; the page alone does not fix it). S is a graded, probably graded-commutative, k-algebra concentrated in degrees >= 0. The context (divided-power de Rham complex, Gamma_*, exterior algebras on the neighbouring pages) suggests S is a divided-power or de Rham type algebra.

Categories and functors.
- M_0 = M^+ is the category of graded S-modules in degrees >= 0.
- N = Mod(k) is the category of k-modules.
- i : N -> M_0 is the induction functor P |-> P (x)_k S.
- Its right adjoint is written k : M |-> M_0, the degree-0 component.
- M_N is most plausibly the category of graded S-modules living in degrees >= N, or equivalently M_0 modulo modules concentrated in degrees < N.
- tau_N = tau_{N,0} : M_0 -> M_N is truncation M |-> M_{>=N}.
- rho_N = rho_{0N} is its right adjoint. Explicitly, rho_N(M')_alpha = Hom^alpha(S_{>=N-alpha}, M'), i.e. the module of 'sections over the punctured spectrum' with respect to the ideal S_{>=N}. This matches the formula in c').

Composite adjunction. The composite i_N = tau_{N,0} o i : Mod k -> M_N has right adjoint k o rho_{0N}. Grothendieck notes k o rho_{0N} = k o tau_0 o rho_N = k o rho_N.

First set of equivalent conditions. These are the standard criterion that a left adjoint is fully faithful iff the unit is an isomorphism, iff the right adjoint is a (Gabriel) localization.
- a) i_N is fully faithful.
- b) For every P, the unit P -> (rho_N i_N P)_0 is an isomorphism. He notes this equals (rho_N tau_N(P (x) S))_0 = (rho_N(P (x)_k tau_N S))_0.
- c) k o rho_N is a localization functor.

Second, stronger set of conditions. Here i itself should factor through the essential image of rho_{0N}:
- a') Im ess i is contained in Im ess rho_{0,N}.
- b') i(P) -> rho_{0N} i_N(P) is an isomorphism for all P.
- b'bis) The same, but checked only in degrees 0 <= alpha <= N-1, since in degrees >= N it is automatic.
- c') For every P and every 0 <= alpha <= N-1, the restriction map P (x)_k S_alpha = Hom^alpha(S, P (x) S) -> Hom^alpha(tau_{N-alpha} S, P (x) S) is an isomorphism.
- The last line is the kernel condition Hom^alpha(S / tau_{N-alpha} S, P (x)_k S) = 0.

Interpretation. The free modules P (x) S must have 'depth >= 2' along the irrelevant-type ideal S_{>=N} in low degrees. Then the whole graded module is recovered from its tail in degrees >= N. This is a Serre/Gabriel-type reconstruction: compare M = Gamma_*(M~) for depth >= 2, and local cohomology H^0, H^1 with supports in S_{>=N} vanishing.

Purpose. Presumably to show that the divided-power (or de Rham) graded object, and k-modules, can be recovered from the truncated category M_N. This is a technical lemma in the 1976 divided-power de Rham lecture notes.
errors: The final line Hom^alpha(S/tau_{N-alpha}S, P(x)S) = 0 is only equivalent to injectivity of the restriction map in c'. By the exact sequence 0 -> Hom(S/tau S, M) -> Hom(S, M) -> Hom(tau S, M) -> Ext^1(S/tau S, M), surjectivity also needs a vanishing of Ext^1 (or H^1 with supports). So, if intended as equivalent to c', the condition is incomplete: depth >= 2, not depth >= 1, is needed. Grothendieck may have intended it only as the first half.
Notation is unstable: tau_{N,0} vs tau_N, rho_{0N} vs rho_N. The functor called 'k' (degree-0 part) shares its letter with the ground ring k.

ideas.what: Induction i(P) = P (x)_k S composed with truncation to degrees >= N, with right adjoint 'degree-0 part of the sections functor'; fully faithful iff the unit is an isomorphism iff the right adjoint is a localization.
ideas.modern_name: Fully faithful left adjoint / reflective localization (Gabriel localization)

ideas.what: Recovering a graded module in low degrees from its tail in degrees >= N via Hom^alpha(S_{>=N-alpha}, -); the vanishing condition Hom(S/S_{>=N-alpha}, P(x)S) = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Depth / local cohomology with respect to S_{>=N}, the ideal transform; Serre's M -> Gamma_*(M~) for depth >= 2
ideas.where_published: SGA 2 (ideal transform, depth conditions), EGA III/IV in the general form; not this specific graded/truncated version

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine category-theoretic and depth-type equivalences: adjunctions, a localization criterion, and a Serre/SGA2-style reconstruction from truncation. They are working lemmas for the divided-power de Rham lectures, with nothing evidently new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: In the top crossed-out line, 'rho' appears in the triple (i, rho, delta); the image suggests (i, p, S) or (i, rho, S), uncertain.
'k(M_0) = M_0' is more plausibly k(M) = M_0, i.e. the degree-0 component functor.
The marginal crossed note is likely 'qui a un adjoint à gauche', crossed out; this is consistent with the transcription.
In the line before c') the image reads 'en degrés alpha dans' followed by 0 <= alpha <= N-1; the second 'en' is a duplicate transcription artefact.
